Feature: Independent control register for each GPIO.
Test Description: Validate GPIO register reset defaults and masked read/write integrity across per-pin and group control/IO/interrupt registers using predefined data patterns, skipping non-readable/non-writable locations by mask and designated skip lists.
Meta Test Description: The test invokes chk_rst_val() to iterate over addr_array[49] and verify default values for all registers not marked in skip_rst_array and with read_mask_array != 0. For each, it reads data_rd = read_reg(addr), masks off bit0 (data = data_rd & 0xFFFFFFFE), and compares to default_value_array[i]. def_fail_cnt increments on mismatch. Next, chk_rd_wr() applies 6 write patterns {0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000}. For each pattern, it iterates writable registers (skip_array[i] == 0 and write_mask_array[i] != 0) to write write_reg(addr, (data_wr & write_mask_array[i])). Then it iterates readable/writable registers (skip_array[i] == 0, write_mask_array[i] != 0, read_mask_array[i] != 0) to read data_rd = (read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]) and compute exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | ((~write_mask_array[i]) & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])). wr_fail_cnt increments on mismatch. At end of test_case(), finish(0) if both counters are zero else finish(1). A soft_reset_chk() is present but compiled-out (#ifdef 0).
Remarks: Skips registers as per skip arrays and when read/write masks are zero. For default checks, bit0 is ignored (masked to 0) before comparison. Ensure GPIO DIN inputs are driven to known stable states; otherwise DIN may read as 1 and not match expected default, per code comment. Group registers flagged as VRRW are skipped during write/read as indicated by the skip arrays.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Initialize the GPIO test and load the register address, default, read-mask, and write-mask tables. 2) For each GPIO-related register, if it is included for reset verification and readable, read its value and compare to the documented default (ignoring bit0). 3) Apply a set of predefined data patterns to all GPIO registers that are writable, respecting each register’s write mask. 4) For each written register that is also readable, read back and compare against the expected value derived from the pattern, read mask, write mask, and stored default. 5) Skip any registers marked by the skip lists or those with non-readable/non-writable masks. 6) Record any mismatches for default or readback comparisons. 7) Report PASS only if no mismatches are found across all checks; otherwise report FAIL.
